requirements.text: The SM-Task Manager application allows users to add tasks through a user-friendly interface. Users can input a task description into the text field identified by the data-testid 'task-input'. Upon entering a valid task description (non-empty and trimmed of leading/trailing spaces), users can either press the 'Enter' key or click the 'Add Task' button, identified by the data-testid 'add-task-btn', to add the task to the task list. The task list is displayed as an unordered list with the data-testid 'task-list'. Each task entry includes the task description, an input for expected completion time, and buttons for marking the task as completed or deleting it. After a task is successfully added, the input field is cleared, and the 'Clear All' button, identified by the data-testid 'clear-all-btn', becomes visible. If the task input is empty or consists solely of spaces, the task is not added, and the 'Clear All' button remains hidden if no tasks exist. The application ensures that the task list is dynamically updated with animations for new entries, and the 'Clear All' button's visibility is contingent on the presence of tasks in the list.

Users can add a task by pressing the 'Enter' key after entering text in the task input field. The task input field is identified by the data-testid 'task-input'. When the user presses the 'Enter' key, the system should trigger the 'Add Task' button click event. If the input contains only whitespace or is empty, no task should be added, and the input field should remain empty. If the input contains valid text, the task should be added to the task list identified by the data-testid 'task-list', with leading and trailing spaces trimmed. After adding the task, the input field should be cleared. The system should ensure that the task list is updated accordingly, and the 'Clear All' button, identified by the data-testid 'clear-all-btn', should be displayed if there are tasks in the list.

The SM-Task Manager web application allows users to manage tasks through a user-friendly interface. Each task entry in the task list includes a 'Completed' button, identifiable by the data-id 'complete-btn', which users can click to toggle the task's completion status. Upon clicking the 'Completed' button, the system visually updates the task by adding or removing the 'completed' class to the task's DOM element, providing immediate feedback on the task's status. This functionality supports toggling for individual tasks as well as multiple tasks simultaneously. The task list is dynamically updated to reflect these changes, ensuring users can efficiently manage their task completion statuses.

The web application must allow users to delete individual tasks from the task list using a 'Delete' button associated with each task entry. The 'Delete' button must be identifiable by the class 'delete-btn' and should be located within each task's container in the task list, which is identified by the data-testid 'task-list'. Upon clicking the 'Delete' button, the system must remove the corresponding task from the DOM. If the task list becomes empty after deletion, the system must hide the 'Clear All' button, which is identified by the data-testid 'clear-all-btn'. The 'Clear All' button should only be visible when there is at least one task in the list. This functionality must handle normal cases where multiple tasks exist, as well as edge cases where the deleted task is the only task in the list.

The SM-Task Manager application allows users to clear all tasks from the task list by interacting with the 'Clear All' button. When the user clicks the 'Clear All' button, identified by the data-testid 'clear-all-btn', the system will remove all tasks from the task list, which is identified by the data-testid 'task-list'. Additionally, the 'Clear All' button will be hidden from view after all tasks are cleared. This functionality is only applicable when there are tasks present in the list. The 'Clear All' button should be visible only when there is at least one task in the list, and it should be hidden when the list is empty, ensuring a clear and intuitive user experience.

The task input field, identified by the data-testid 'task-input' and id 'task-input', must display the placeholder text 'Enter a new task...' when the 'SM-Task Manager' page is fully loaded. This placeholder guides users in entering new tasks. No user action is required for this placeholder to be visible; it should be present by default upon page load. The placeholder text should remain visible until the user begins typing in the input field.

reference_cases.title: [Normal] Add a task successfully
reference_cases.description:
Feature: Task Addition Functionality
  Users can add a task by clicking the 'Add Task' button. The task should be added to the task list, the input field should be cleared, and the 'Clear All' button should be displayed.


  Scenario: [Normal] Add a task successfully
    Given the SM-Task Manager page is loaded
    And the task input field with data-testid "task-input" is empty
    When the user enters "Buy groceries" into the task input field with data-testid "task-input"
    And the user clicks the 'Add Task' button with data-testid "add-task-btn"
    Then the task list with data-testid "task-list" should contain a task with the text "Buy groceries"
    And the task input field with data-testid "task-input" should be empty
    And the 'Clear All' button with data-testid "clear-all-btn" should be displayed

reference_cases.title: [Edge] Add a task with leading and trailing spaces
reference_cases.description:
Feature: Task Addition Functionality
  Users can add a task by clicking the 'Add Task' button. The task should be added to the task list, the input field should be cleared, and the 'Clear All' button should be displayed.


  Scenario: [Edge] Add a task with leading and trailing spaces
    Given the SM-Task Manager page is loaded
    And the task input field with data-testid "task-input" is empty
    When the user enters "   Call mom   " into the task input field with data-testid "task-input"
    And the user clicks the 'Add Task' button with data-testid "add-task-btn"
    Then the task list with data-testid "task-list" should contain a task with the text "Call mom"
    And the task input field with data-testid "task-input" should be empty
    And the 'Clear All' button with data-testid "clear-all-btn" should be displayed

reference_cases.title: [Error] Attempt to add an empty task
reference_cases.description:
Feature: Task Addition Functionality
  Users can add a task by clicking the 'Add Task' button. The task should be added to the task list, the input field should be cleared, and the 'Clear All' button should be displayed.


  Scenario: [Error] Attempt to add an empty task
    Given the SM-Task Manager page is loaded
    And the task input field with data-testid "task-input" is empty
    When the user clicks the 'Add Task' button with data-testid "add-task-btn"
    Then the task list with data-testid "task-list" should remain empty
    And the task input field with data-testid "task-input" should be empty
    And the 'Clear All' button with data-testid "clear-all-btn" should not be displayed

reference_cases.title: [Edge] Add a task using the 'Enter' key with leading and trailing spaces
reference_cases.description:
Feature: REQ-003 - Add Task Using 'Enter' Key
  Users can add a task by pressing the 'Enter' key after entering text in the task input field.


  Scenario: [Edge] Add a task using the 'Enter' key with leading and trailing spaces
    Given the SM-Task Manager page is loaded
    And the task input field with data-testid "task-input" is empty
    When the user enters "   Finish homework   " into the task input field with data-testid "task-input"
    And presses the 'Enter' key
    Then the task "Finish homework" should be added to the task list with data-testid "task-list"
    And the task input field with data-testid "task-input" should be cleared

reference_cases.title: [Error] Attempt to add an empty task using the 'Enter' key
reference_cases.description:
Feature: REQ-003 - Add Task Using 'Enter' Key
  Users can add a task by pressing the 'Enter' key after entering text in the task input field.


  Scenario: [Error] Attempt to add an empty task using the 'Enter' key
    Given the SM-Task Manager page is loaded
    And the task input field with data-testid "task-input" is empty
    When the user presses the 'Enter' key
    Then no task should be added to the task list with data-testid "task-list"
    And the task input field with data-testid "task-input" should remain empty

reference_cases.title: [Normal] Toggle task completion status
reference_cases.description:
Feature: Task Completion Toggle
  Each task entry includes a 'Completed' button to toggle its completion status. Users can view tasks in the list and click the 'Completed' button on a task to change its visual completion status.


  Scenario: [Normal] Toggle task completion status
    Given the SM-Task Manager page is loaded
    And the user enters "Buy groceries" into the task input field with data-testid "task-input"
    And the user clicks the "Add Task" button with data-testid "add-task-btn"
    When the user clicks the "Completed" button on the task "Buy groceries" with data-id "complete-btn"
    Then the task "Buy groceries" should have the class "completed"

reference_cases.title: [Edge] Toggle completion status of multiple tasks
reference_cases.description:
Feature: Task Completion Toggle
  Each task entry includes a 'Completed' button to toggle its completion status. Users can view tasks in the list and click the 'Completed' button on a task to change its visual completion status.


  Scenario: [Edge] Toggle completion status of multiple tasks
    Given the SM-Task Manager page is loaded
    And the user enters "Buy groceries" into the task input field with data-testid "task-input"
    And the user clicks the "Add Task" button with data-testid "add-task-btn"
    And the user enters "Walk the dog" into the task input field with data-testid "task-input"
    And the user clicks the "Add Task" button with data-testid "add-task-btn"
    When the user clicks the "Completed" button on the task "Buy groceries" with data-id "complete-btn"
    And the user clicks the "Completed" button on the task "Walk the dog" with data-id "complete-btn"
    Then both tasks "Buy groceries" and "Walk the dog" should have the class "completed"

reference_cases.title: [Normal] User deletes a task from the list
reference_cases.description:
Feature: Task Deletion Functionality
  The system allows users to delete individual tasks from the task list. Upon deletion, the system checks if the 'Clear All' button should be hidden when no tasks remain.


  Scenario: [Normal] User deletes a task from the list
    Given the SM-Task Manager page is loaded
    And the user enters "Buy groceries" into the task input field with data-testid "task-input"
    And the user clicks the "Add Task" button with data-testid "add-task-btn"
    And the task "Buy groceries" is displayed in the task list with data-testid "task-list"
    When the user clicks the "Delete" button for the task "Buy groceries"
    Then the task "Buy groceries" should be removed from the task list
    And the "Clear All" button with data-testid "clear-all-btn" should be hidden

reference_cases.title: [Edge] User deletes the only task in the list
reference_cases.description:
Feature: Task Deletion Functionality
  The system allows users to delete individual tasks from the task list. Upon deletion, the system checks if the 'Clear All' button should be hidden when no tasks remain.


  Scenario: [Edge] User deletes the only task in the list
    Given the SM-Task Manager page is loaded
    And the user enters "Read a book" into the task input field with data-testid "task-input"
    And the user clicks the "Add Task" button with data-testid "add-task-btn"
    And the task "Read a book" is displayed in the task list with data-testid "task-list"
    When the user clicks the "Delete" button for the task "Read a book"
    Then the task "Read a book" should be removed from the task list
    And the "Clear All" button with data-testid "clear-all-btn" should be hidden

reference_cases.title: [Normal] Clear all tasks when tasks are present
reference_cases.description:
Feature: Clear All Tasks Functionality
  Users can clear all tasks by clicking the 'Clear All' button to remove all tasks from the list and hide the 'Clear All' button.


  Scenario: [Normal] Clear all tasks when tasks are present
    Given the SM-Task Manager page is loaded
    And the user enters "Task 1" into the task input field with data-testid "task-input"
    And the user clicks the "Add Task" button with data-testid "add-task-btn"
    And the user enters "Task 2" into the task input field with data-testid "task-input"
    And the user clicks the "Add Task" button with data-testid "add-task-btn"
    When the user clicks the "Clear All" button with data-testid "clear-all-btn"
    Then the task list with data-testid "task-list" should be empty
    And the "Clear All" button with data-testid "clear-all-btn" should not be visible

reference_cases.title: [Normal] Display placeholder text in task input field
reference_cases.description:
Feature: Task Input Field Placeholder Text
  The task input field provides a placeholder text to guide task entry.


  Scenario: [Normal] Display placeholder text in task input field
    Given the user is on the "SM-Task Manager" page
    When the page is fully loaded
    Then the task input field with data-testid "task-input" should display the placeholder text "Enter a new task..."
